selection_rationale: Italy is one of the largest EU and NATO economies and a major European manufacturing, fiscal, energy and Mediterranean actor, yet the public corpus lacks a reusable country dossier. Existing European security research and Germany/France country contexts require Italian context to analyse European industrial capacity, defence burden-sharing, euro-area fiscal transmission, energy security and the post-RRF investment cycle without rebuilding the same structural background.
contrary_evidence: High public debt, weak productivity and adverse demographics support a low-growth structural-risk thesis, but a deep manufacturing base, non-energy trade surpluses, record employment and a resilient banking system argue against a simple decline narrative.
Italy's small-firm structure can constrain innovation and scaling, while industrial districts demonstrate that networks of specialised SMEs can also generate durable export competitiveness.

Rapid renewable-capacity growth reduces energy vulnerability, but natural gas, imported fossil fuels and electricity imports remain material, so energy independence is not yet an accurate description.

Recent faster employment growth in the South shows convergence is possible, but long-standing regional gaps in participation, productivity and infrastructure remain too large to treat the North-South divide as resolved.
limitations: 2026 GDP, employment, trade and demographic observations are provisional and can be revised.
Debt projections differ across the IMF, European Commission and Italian authorities because assumptions and stock-flow treatments differ.
PNRR disbursements, realised spending, completed projects and productivity impact are separate measures and should not be used interchangeably.
NATO and national COFOG defence-spending definitions have different accounting perimeters and cannot be added or compared without adjustment.
Installed renewable capacity does not equal usable annual generation and must be interpreted alongside grids, storage, imports and thermal balancing.
National and macro-regional averages conceal substantial variation among Italian regions and municipalities.

en.title: Italy: manufacturing depth, high public debt and the demographic limits of the euro-era growth model
en.deck: Italy combines deep manufacturing and persistent non-energy trade surpluses with very high public debt, weak productivity and adverse demographics; the structural test is whether the €194.4 billion recovery plan can lift potential growth before ageing and interest costs absorb the fiscal space.
en.regime: Export-capable manufacturing economy inside the euro area, with improving fiscal credibility but structurally weak productivity, high public debt and demographic decline making post-PNRR reform persistence decisive.
en.key_risk: A post-PNRR investment and governance cliff combined with ageing, energy dependence and rising interest or defence costs could keep nominal growth too weak to place public debt on a durable downward path.

pt-BR.title: Itália: profundidade manufatureira, dívida pública elevada e limites demográficos do modelo de crescimento da era do euro
pt-BR.deck: A Itália combina manufatura profunda e superávit comercial não energético persistente com dívida pública muito elevada, produtividade fraca e demografia adversa; o teste estrutural é se o plano de recuperação de €194,4 bilhões consegue elevar o crescimento potencial antes que envelhecimento e juros absorvam o espaço fiscal.
pt-BR.regime: Economia manufatureira exportadora dentro da área do euro, com melhora de credibilidade fiscal, mas produtividade estruturalmente fraca, dívida pública elevada e declínio demográfico tornando decisiva a continuidade das reformas após o PNRR.
pt-BR.key_risk: Uma queda do investimento e da capacidade de governança após o PNRR, combinada a envelhecimento, dependência energética e custos maiores de juros ou defesa, pode manter o crescimento nominal baixo demais para colocar a dívida em trajetória duradoura de queda.
